profile.summary: RITA is a family of four generative protein language models that read a protein sequence one amino acid at a time, left to right. They were trained on over 280 million sequences from UniRef-100 to predict the next amino acid. They can generate new sequences from a prompt, and the likelihood they assign to a sequence can be used as a zero-shot fitness score for mutants.

summary_quotes.text: a suite of autoregressive generative models for protein sequences, with up to 1.2 billion parameters, trained on over 280 million protein sequences belonging to the UniRef-100 database
we evaluate RITA models in next amino acid prediction, zero-shot fitness, and enzyme function prediction
Main script to score sets of mutated protein sequences (substitutions or indels) with RITA models.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Each RITA model is a decoder-only transformer trained as a causal language model: given the residues so far, it predicts the next one. The four sizes share this design and differ in width and depth, from 768 dimensions and 12 layers (Small) to 2048 dimensions and 24 layers (XLarge). The paper studies how next amino acid prediction, zero-shot fitness and enzyme function prediction change with model size. For fitness, the repository's script scores each mutated sequence by its log-likelihood under the model, summed over the sequence read forwards and backwards.
sections.source_locator: arXiv abstract; README: model table; config.json; compute_fitness.py

quotes.text: We conduct the first systematic study of how capabilities evolve with model size for autoregressive transformers in the protein domain
Model | #Params | d_model | layers | lm loss uniref-100

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: There are four checkpoints, each a separate Hugging Face repository. The README reports a language-model loss on UniRef-100 that falls with size, from 2.31 (Small) to 1.70 (XLarge). A result should name the size and the Hugging Face revision. This page read RITA_s at revision 818eb05a; the API revisions for the others are in the saved responses. Weights are stored in float16.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Autoregressive (left-to-right) generative protein language model, a family of four sizes.

quotes.text: RITA is a family of autoregressive protein models
a suite of autoregressive generative models for protein sequences

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Decoder-only transformer with a causal language model head. Per the configs: RITA-S d_model 768, 12 layers, 12 heads; Medium 1024, 24 layers, 16 heads; Large 1536, 24 layers, 24 heads; XLarge 2048, 24 layers, 32 heads.
facts.source_locator: README: model table; config.json of all four checkpoints

quotes.text: autoregressive transformers in the protein domain

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A protein sequence as amino acid letters, tokenised by the RITA tokenizer (vocabulary of 26 tokens in the RITA-S config). For generation, a sequence prefix used as the prompt.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Next-token logits. These give generated sequences through the text-generation pipeline, or a sequence log-likelihood that compute_fitness.py uses as a zero-shot fitness score (the negative cross-entropy over the sequence and its reverse).

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: 85M (Small), 300M (Medium), 680M (Large), 1.2B (XLarge), as the README prints them. Hugging Face counts from the safetensors files: RITA_s 85,096,320; RITA_m 302,365,440; RITA_xl 1,208,709,888; no count is shown for RITA_l.
facts.source_locator: README: model table; Hugging Face API responses

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Over 280 million protein sequences from the UniRef-100 database.

quotes.text: trained on over 280 million protein sequences belonging to the UniRef-100 database

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: Four checkpoints on Hugging Face: lightonai/RITA_s (Small), RITA_m (Medium), RITA_l (Large) and RITA_xl (XLarge).

facts.label: Training cutoff
facts.value: Not extracted. The abstract names UniRef-100 but not its release, and the full paper was not read.

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: 1,024 tokens (max_seq_len in all four configs). The fitness script splits longer proteins into windows of 1,023 residues.
facts.source_locator: config.json of all four checkpoints; compute_fitness.py calc_fitness

facts.label: Weights licence
facts.value: None declared. The Hugging Face model card metadata lists tags and the dataset but no licence; the paper says the models are released openly.

strengths.text: Needs only a single sequence: no alignment or structure is required to score or generate.
Four sizes from 85M to 1.2B parameters, so cost can be traded against accuracy; the paper reports benefits from scale (the authors' claim).
The scoring script handles insertions and deletions as well as substitutions, because it scores whole sequences.

quotes.text: help='Whether to score sequences with insertions and deletions'

strengths.text: Code is MIT licensed and the weights are not gated.

quotes.text: Permission is hereby granted, free of charge

limitations.text: Context is 1,024 tokens; longer proteins must be split into windows, which the fitness script does.
No licence is declared for the weights on Hugging Face.

Loading needs custom model code from the Hugging Face repository (trust_remote_code=True), and the repository gives no environment file or library versions; the config was saved with transformers 4.18.0.
The fitness script moves the model to a CUDA device, so it expects a GPU as written.

run_guide.summary: Get the repository at a pinned commit and generate two short protein sequences with RITA-S using the repository's example script.
prerequisites: Python with PyTorch and the Hugging Face transformers library. The sources give no versions; the RITA-S config was saved with transformers 4.18.0.
Internet access to download the weights from Hugging Face. GPU need for generation is not stated.
Code is MIT licensed; no licence is declared for the weights.

steps.title: Get the code at the pinned commit
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/lightonai/RITA.git
cd RITA
git checkout --detach 20b2b55f6e098bb9f69c37d96159a0ee1f0d631d
steps.explanation: The README gives no clone command; these lines get the repository at the commit this page was written from.

steps.title: Generate sequences
steps.explanation: example.py loads lightonai/RITA_s and its tokenizer and samples two sequences of up to 20 tokens from the prompt MAB. Use it instead of the README snippet, which omits the AutoTokenizer import.

outputs: Two lines, each starting with seq: followed by a generated amino acid sequence with spaces removed.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
Install commands are not given in the sources; PyTorch and transformers must be installed separately.
Zero-shot fitness scoring uses compute_fitness.py, which needs a ProteinGym reference file and DMS folder and a CUDA GPU; its run is not included here.

notes: RITA_l has no safetensors count on Hugging Face, so its structured parameters value is the README's 680M. The model card's usage snippet has a misplaced quote ("lightonai/RITA_s, trust_remote_code=True"); the repository README and example.py have it right. released is the date the host records for the weights (the Hugging Face createdAt field, 2022-04-25 for all four), the same rule used for the other models in this batch; it is an upload date, not necessarily the training date.
